item.title: Colombia podría dar más tiempo para emitir las normas del open finance
item.description: Colombia podría tardar un poco más de lo esperado en llegar a la meta del open finance . El Ministerio de Finanzas quiere aprobar un decreto que propone dar seis meses más a la Superintendencia Financiera (SFC) para publicar los plazos de implementación de cuatro aspectos clave del modelo : la adopción de estándares tecnológicos y de seguridad , la activación del directorio de participantes , la definición de los indicadores de seguimiento y la fijación de estándares de la portabilidad financiera. Accede al análisis que impulsa la toma de decisiones en la banca latinoamericana Este contenido exclusivo está disponible solo para miembros registrados de iupana.

item.title: Matter Intelligence Debuts Roof-Condition Platform
item.description: We’re giving insurers a way to bring the condition of the asset itself into their risk decisions.” Physical Condition as a Risk Signal According to Matter, the platform can support underwriting by assessing roof condition at the point of quote, reducing reliance on physical inspections and referrals. (Image credit: IIR.) Matter Intelligence (London) plans to unveil a space-based property intelligence solution for insurers at ITC Vegas 2026, combining spectral sensing and AI to assess the physical condition of residential roofs at scale. Vishnu Sridhar, Co-Founder and CEO, Matter Intelligence.

item.title: MGAs Can Differentiate by Closing the Data Trust Gap
item.description: Carriers bear the risk but depend on data produced closest to it by MGAs. As a growing share of delegated business flows through MGAs outside carrier ownership, an MGA that requires extensive data reconstruction becomes more vulnerable to being deprioritized. From Data Delivery to Data Confidence For forward-looking MGAs, this is not simply a volume problem.

item.title: GM Faces Down Fuel Prices With Big Trucks and Bigger Engines
item.description: GM will be starting production of the trucks and bigger engines just as fuel prices have risen to nearly $5 a gallon and diesel prices hit a record. Despite steep fuel prices, Chevrolet Vice President Scott Bell says the company is adding production of V-8 engines and elevated trucks that are raised up for off-road driving because consumers want more than GM can currently build. Forget about starry-eyed goals to go all electric by 2035 that once anchored Chief Executive Officer Mary Barra’s goal of doubling revenue: The company runs on truck profits, and the all-new versions of the Silverado and Sierra will come with bigger engines and a plan to produce even more of them.

item.title: AM Best: US Mutual Insurers Doubled Net Income in 2025
item.description: property/casualty mutual insurers doubled compared to 2024 to about $42.6 billion in 2025 as underwriting income surged to about $14.8 billion from a loss of $7.2 billion in 2024. Best report on the segment, the rise in net income was also driven by a modest 2% decline in loss and loss adjustment expenses despite underwriting expenses increasing 5.8% in 2025 compared to the year prior. The list of top mutual insurers typically does not move much from year to year and that was the same in 2025, with the top 25 accounting for more than 83% of total NPW from mutuals.

item.title: Wisedocs Launches Legal Intelligence at ITC Vegas 2026, Giving Insurance Defense Teams AI Analysis of the Full Claim File, Starting with Depositions and Demand Letters
item.description: Legal Intelligence enables insurance defense teams to analyze legal documents — starting with deposition transcripts and demand letters — against a claims organization’s verified medical records and claim history, giving claims professionals and defense counsel a single view of what was said under oath, what is being claimed in the demand, and what the medical evidence and claimant history actually show. View Series New early-access Wisedocs AI product cross-references legal documents — starting with deposition transcripts and demand letters — against verified medical records and claim history, built only for the insurance defense side of the claim. Unveiled at ITC Vegas 2026 , Wisedocs, the leading claims decision intelligence platform , today announces the launch of Wisedocs Legal Intelligence , now available in early access, bringing the disjointed medical and legal sides of a claim together.

item.title: Marsh launches Archer platform for life and annuity reinsurers, sidecars, SPIs and cells
item.description: With the life and annuity reinsurance space seeing a wave of interest from both internal and external sponsors, including third-party capital providers, Marsh has launched a new platform initiative named Archer that is designed to help sponsors quickly set up and launch a new life and annuity reinsurance structure including sidecars. Those structures can ultimately range from standalone reinsurance vehicles, through life and annuity reinsurance sidecars, including special purpose reinsurers, dedicated reinsurance cells and standalone segregated accounts, Marsh said. Archer by Marsh is a new service and platform to support asset managers and life and annuity insurers as they establish and operate reinsurance businesses, leveraging Marsh’s shared operating infrastructure while the sponsors retain ownership and strategic control.

item.title: Catastrophe bond soft market not yet at 2017 levels, but could last another year: Lane Financial
item.description: In its last analysis of the catastrophe bond market earlier this year, Lane Financial had said that the outstanding market yield of non-impaired natural cat bonds was no longer as soft as it had been at the end of 2025, but the firm also highlighted that investor returns had been eroded by falling secondary market prices . The current soft market in catastrophe bonds and insurance-linked securities (ILS) is not yet at the depressed levels seen in 2017, analysis from consultancy Lane Financial LLC shows. But the company suggests the soft cat bond market could last another year, if 2026 continues to run loss-free.

item.title: ILS fund gains accelerate, cat bonds particularly strong. Average August return 1.39%: ILS Advisers
item.description: Insurance-linked securities investment fund strategies, across catastrophe bonds and private ILS, saw returns accelerating in August 2026, as the average ILS fund performance reached 1.39% and cat bond funds had a particularly strong month, latest data from the ILS Advisers Fund Index shows. For August 2026, ILS Advisers reports the average return across its index constituent ILS funds was 1.39%, which now becomes the best month of the year and the strongest single month of ILS fund performance since October 2025 for this Index. For 2026, August’s performance lifts the average ILS fund return for the year so far to 6.56%, which continues to run at a slightly above average level despite the softening of the reinsurance market.

item.title: SiriusPoint and Sutton Special Risk launch new sport insurance product for colleges and universities
item.description: SiriusPoint, a specialty underwriter, has announced a new strategic partnership with Sutton Special Risk, a specialist managing general underwriter providing innovative accident and health insurance solutions, to launch a new insurance product, SportsSecure™. By combining their complementary strengths in underwriting, specialised insurance, and sports-related accident and health expertise, SiriusPoint and Sutton Special Risk aim to support brokers, colleges, and universities as they navigate the evolving NIL and revenue-sharing landscape. Sutton Special Risk brings that expertise, and together we are offering a thoughtful, specialized way to manage injury-related financial exposure and protect the long-term stability of their athletic programs.” “We are excited to partner with SiriusPoint to bring a dedicated solution to an increasingly important segment of the collegiate sports market,” said Christian Hanson, VP Sports at Sutton Special Risk.

item.title: HDI Global Belgium establishes aviation underwriting team for Benelux and Southern Europe
item.description: HDI Global Belgium, the Belgian business of international commercial and industrial insurer HDI Global, has created a dedicated Aviation underwriting team to serve brokers and clients across the Benelux and Southern European markets. Based in Brussels and led by Stijn Keppens, the new team sits within HDI Global’s Specialty aviation business and is intended to provide regional market access to the company’s wider aviation underwriting capabilities. “The launch of this team marks an important step in strengthening HDI’s specialist aviation capabilities across Europe,” commented Jamie Bowes, Global Head of Aviation at HDI Global.

item.title: Global Atlantic appoints Dan Farrelly as Head of IMO and IBD Channels
item.description: Global Atlantic, a provider of retirement security and investment solutions and a wholly-owned subsidiary of KKR, has announced the appointment of Dan Farrelly as Head of Independent Marketing Organization (IMO) and Independent Broker-Dealer (IBD) Channels. Based in New York City, Farrelly will lead Global Atlantic’s relationships across the IMO and IBD channels, working closely with distribution partners to identify opportunities for growth and expand access to Global Atlantic’s retirement strategies. Farrelly joins Global Atlantic from Prosperity Life, where he served as SVP, Head of Annuity Distribution.

item.title: Estonia Says Russia Behind Arson Attack on Defense Firm
item.description: Estonia’s government said with “full confidence” that Russian special services commissioned an August arson attack against a defense manufacturing facility in Tallinn. “The arson attack on Milrem in Estonia on the night of 15 August was an act of sabotage,” Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal said in a press release on Tuesday. Read more: Russia’s Attacks on Europe Are Getting More Brazen and More Dangerous Estonian officials said the attack on the company that supplies unmanned vehicles to Ukraine is part of a broader Russian campaign of sabotage and aggression across Europe to deter support for Kyiv.

item.title: Samsung’s Insurance Arms Lead Korean Drive for Overseas M&A
item.description: South Korean banks and insurers are hunting for overseas deals to lift growth, signaling a broader outward turn by an industry that largely stayed home while companies including Samsung Electronics Co. Korean executives are studying the decades-long overseas expansion of Japanese financial institutions, hoping to replicate their successes while dodging the costly acquisitions and difficult integrations that accompanied some investments in emerging Asia. Read more: Tokio Marine Weighs More Than $10 Billion of International M&A “Going overseas is becoming almost unavoidable for Korean financial firms because the domestic market is mature and demographics are deteriorating,” said Jongmin Shim, Seoul-based head of research at CLSA Securities.

item.title: French Court Finds Swiftair Guilty of Corporate Manslaughter Over Mali Crash
item.description: The Paris Criminal Court found Spanish company Swiftair guilty of corporate manslaughter on Monday over the 2014 crash of an Air Algerie flight that killed 116 people in northern Mali. However, a French judge ordered the company to pay the maximum fine in France of €225,000 for corporate manslaughter, “or involuntary homicide,” after a three-week trial earlier this year over the crash of a Swiftair-owned MD-83 airliner. During the rare corporate manslaughter trial, prosecutors alleged negligence in the way Swiftair pilots were trained to deal with icy conditions and erratic data.

item.title: People Moves: BevCap Adds Gross as Business Development Executive

Gross brings more than 18 years of insurance industry experience, with a career spanning both the carrier and brokerage sectors. He held middle-market roles with Sentry Insurance and Huntington Bank, where he developed extensive expertise in client and broker engagement before transitioning into the captive insurance space with Garnet Captive.

item.title: First Wild Screwworm Fly Detected in Texas Since Outbreak Began
item.description: The US Department of Agriculture has caught its first wild screwworm fly since the parasite was detected in the country’s livestock nearly four months ago, signaling the potential for continued spread even as overall cases have remained muted. The wild screwworm fly was detected in Brewster County, Texas, on Friday. The agency said in a Saturday post on X that it places traps “just outside of infested areas to avoid capturing sterile flies and better pinpoint where wild flies may be moving.” 🚨 USDA has confirmed the first wild New World screwworm fly in a trap in Brewster County, Texas.

item.title: Michigan Transportation Company Sued for Sexual Harassment
item.description: Davis Cartage Co., a transportation, warehousing and logistics company headquartered in Corunna, Michigan, violated federal law by allowing its president of logistics to sexually harass two female employees at its Owosso, Michigan location, the U.S. Such alleged conduct violates Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which prohibits discrimination based on the basis of sex, including sexual harassment. According to the EEOC’s lawsuit, in 2023, the president of logistics, who is also on the board of directors and part owner of the company, passed over more qualified applicants to hire two young women whose photos he found on social media.

item.title: The Impact of Claims Experiences on Trust
item.description: There's no new data on that subject, but an analysis from earlier in the decade that shows a 30% boost in trust from eliminating bad claims experiences deserves some attention. 43.3% in Spring 2017—and several encouraging nuggets of information about the impact of claims on trust levels. Research also bears out the connection between seeing insurance in action—during the claims process—and the level of trust customers have in their insurers.

item.title: AI Fuels 440% Surge in Hackers Using Blockchains in Attacks
item.description: Open-source artificial intelligence is making it easier for hackers to hide malicious code on blockchains, opening a new front in a crypto industry already grappling with rising cybercrime. In the attacks documented by the report, hackers use a blockchain to leave instructions for that software, such as the location of the server that controls it, a technique known as a “blockchain dead drop.” This can make an attack harder to stop because information recorded on a blockchain cannot be easily removed. Blockchains are typically not involved in the initial infection of a machine, which often happens through conventional means such as supply-chain attacks or malicious downloads, Eric Jardine, head of research at Chainalysis, said in response to questions over email.

item.title: Reinsurance rate declines may slow by 2028, soft market floor may not be found till 2030: Jefferies
item.description: Analysts from Jefferies are not confident that reinsurance leadership teams are fully-acknowledging how fast rates have been softening and believe that the focus will shift to terms and conditions from 2028, while a soft market floor may not be found until 2030. From 2028, when the expected slow-down in rate softening occurs, the Jefferies team expect that, “Thereafter, we expect softening to be on the terms and conditions, which tend to deteriorate late in a cycle, once reinsurers can no longer afford to give up premium income.” Adding that, “We eventually expect prices and terms to find a floor in 2030.” Pricing is deteriorating faster than management teams had expected, the Jefferies team believe, with third-party capital seen as one factor. “In our view, the pace of decline will accelerate next year, and only start to slow in 2028.” In a similar fashion to the softening of the reinsurance market, particularly in US property catastrophe risks, through the 2010’s, the Jefferies team expect that once reinsurers begin to appreciate just how much the reduction in pricing is affecting their premium income, the focus will shift towards a quickening of the relaxation of terms and conditions.

This new video features the opening panel discussion of the day at our recent Artemis London 2026 catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities conference, a session exploring how Lloyd’s market participants are accessing institutional investor capital through the UK based ILS structure London Bridge. Watch the full video from our Artemis London 2026 conference to learn more about how Lloyd’s market participants and institutional investors are utilising the London Bridge ILS structures to connect risk and capital efficiently .

item.title: Casualty sidecar growth to continue. Collateralized reinsurance to see greater flexibility: AM Best
item.description: The reinsurance sidecar market is expected to continue expanding thanks to notable momentum being seen in casualty sidecar structures, according to rating agency AM Best. The firm also highlights that the broader collateralized reinsurance space is poised for future expansion due to greater flexibility in structure, modeling, and perils. The property and casualty sidecar market is a key segment within the insurance-linked securities (ILS) sector that has witnessed prominent growth in recent years.

item.title: UK Monitored Threats and Raised Security at Base Before Incident
item.description: UK authorities were closely monitoring increased threats to a British airbase used by the US and had tightened security at the site before an attempted attack was foiled, according to people familiar with the matter.Five men were arrested on Sunday on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire in an incident that investigators are considering a serious attempted attack. However, a local farmer told British media that she had seen a group of men wearing balaclavas near the base just after midnight on Sunday and called the police, raising questions about whether the plot was on the radar of the security services. While British authorities were watching for threats to the base, according to the people familiar with the matter, who asked not to named discussing an ongoing investigations, they still credited the member of the public with alerting police to the suspects’ presence near the sensitive facility on Sunday morning.
